shouldFix.title: An input corpus whose two initial states contain no initial state
shouldFix.finding: The purpose is to 'Continue leftover-design of OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING by naming initial states of the two live G19 v1 corpus classes', and whatIsAuthored claims 'Two named initial states'. Each record holds exactly four fields: an id that is a slug of the class name, memberVerbatim which is the class name, fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED, and assertsNamedNotAuthored which is a one-element list containing the class name again. There is no state-class, operation, platform, mutation kind or negative test — no condition of any sort. The two records are distinguished only by which class they restate, so nothing here says what state a G19 harness would start in.
shouldFix.againstTheDocumentClass: Four sibling input corpora carry substantive per-state content: permission-fx5-input-corpus.v2 gives four states each with a named revocation position; permission-fx11-input-corpus.v2 gives a state with crashBetween ICI and ICO and its behavioural flags; doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v3 gives fourteen states with variantClass, degradedCase, consentClass and auditWrite; permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2 gives two states with race, outcome and whyDeterministic. In each, the NOT-AUTHORED markers hang off a state that has been named. Here they hang off nothing.
shouldFix.addsNothingOverTheCatalogItConsumes: g19-named-corpus-catalog.v1, already accepted and pinned here, carries per class an id, memberVerbatim, exactByteIntentVerbatim, passPropertyVerbatim and fixtureBytes. This artifact's per-state fields are a strict subset. On the state axis it advances OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING's leftover-design by nothing a later authoring cycle could not already read from the catalog.
shouldFix.theMaterialWasAvailableAndNotForbidden: The defence that matters here is that naming a G19 initial state would require inventing a grant-journal, an inherit-blocked envelope, a monotonic window or a sealed-Run class, all of which the dispatch forbids. I tested it against G19 v1's own namedCorpusClasses and it fails. For the lifecycle-matrix class the source enumerates two included preview state-classes — Rebuildable cache/index and Operational metadata — the slash-joined operation set {migration, backup, purge, recovery}, and the four D-002 platforms, while expressly excluding Authoritative evidence and a sealed-Run class as cells. For the cross-class-mutations class it enumerates file 04's four named negative tests: cross-class writes, cache-to-authority promotion, undeclared Plan inputs, and component evidence commits. Those four are precisely the shape of permission-fx5's four revocation positions, and none of them is a journal, an envelope, a window or a sealed-Run class. The artifact pins the source that contains them and carried none.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing stated is false, no row moves, required-now is untouched, the artifact binds NOTHING and is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, and every prohibition is honoured. The defect is that the deliverable is empty against its own stated purpose.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Give each record at least one named initial state drawn from G19 v1's exactByteIntent — the two state-classes crossed with the four lifecycle operations, and file 04's four named negative tests are already enumerated there — with the NOT-AUTHORED markers attached to those named states rather than to the class name.
shouldFix.notAssertedByThisFinding: I do not author any initial state, propose fixture bytes, name a journal, envelope, window or sealed-Run class, or assert how many states each class should carry.

The larger risk in this cycle is not prior participation but sequence: I rejected a structurally identical artifact immediately before this one, which makes repeating the verdict the path of least effort. I answered that by treating the availability test as the decisive question and running it fresh against G19's own namedCorpusClasses rather than reasoning from the G16 result. coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Sixteen attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject c65f787e at 0444, 5219 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and the artifact's own head field equals it; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-124 token OPEN; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce, and the artifact contains exactly nine 64-hex strings, all of them those pins. Every prohibition is honoured and I tested them by value rather than keyword: zero fixture paths, zero journal fields, zero envelope fields, zero window or duration literals of any unit, no sealed-Run class definition, and zero occurrences of SATISFIED or QUALIFIED. The refusal to steal the DR-124 leftovers is accurate — state-class-leftover-join.v2 carries OBL-GRANT-JOURNAL, OBL-INHERIT-BLOCKED, OBL-MONOTONIC and OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING all at leftoverDesign true, which I read at source. The two classes are identical four ways and the slash-joined operation set is held whole rather than split. The finding is the artifact's own deliverable. It exists to name initial states — its purpose field and its whatIsAuthored claim both say so — and its two records contain none: each holds a slug of the class name, the class name, a NOT-AUTHORED marker, and the class name again, so the two are distinguished only by which class they restate. Four sibling input corpora carry real per-state content, and this artifact is also a strict subset of the catalog it consumes, which carries exactByteIntentVerbatim and passPropertyVerbatim per class. This is the second consecutive input corpus I have rejected on this defect, so the coordinator should know how I guarded against simply repeating myself. The decisive question is whether the gate's classes admit namable states without inventing something the dispatch forbids, and I ran that test fresh against G19's own namedCorpusClasses rather than reasoning from the G16 result. It fails here for reasons entirely specific to G19: the source enumerates two included preview state-classes, Rebuildable cache/index and Operational metadata, crossed with the slash-joined operation set migration, backup, purge, recovery, on four D-002 platforms, expressly excluding Authoritative evidence and a sealed-Run class as cells; and for the second class it enumerates file 04's four named negative tests — cross-class writes, cache-to-authority promotion, undeclared Plan inputs, and component evidence commits. Not one of those is a grant-journal, an inherit-blocked envelope, a monotonic window or a sealed-Run class, and the four negative tests are precisely the shape of permission-fx5's four revocation positions. The material was in a source the artifact pins. Had that test resolved the other way — had the only namable states been expressible solely as forbidden objects — the thinness would have been forced and this would have been an ACCEPT. It is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because nothing stated is false and OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING remains open on both the gate join and the row join. Two things declined and recorded: the artifact calls itself 'this catalog' three times while being an input corpus, which has a precedent I accepted at doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v3; and it carries no recordedInputs or remeasurementClause, which is the input-corpus form as the dispatch's own head-field phrasing reflects.
